title: Alibaba Qwen AI Glasses OTA Update: Real-Time Translation Now Available for Calls and Video Watching

content_html:
A pair of glasses perched on your nose is trying to knock down the language barrier for you. On November 2, Alibaba's Qwen AI glasses rolled out an OTA update that moves "real-time translation" from your phone to right in front of your eyes—when you make calls or join cross-border meetings, it can translate what the other person says into your native language in real time at your ear; when you listen to overseas podcasts, take foreign-language online courses, or grind through foreign-language movies, translations also appear in real time in the companion Qwen AI wearable app. Compared with holding up your phone to read translations, the glasses-on-your-face form factor frees up your hands and lets you keep up with the rhythm of conversation more naturally.

Dual-track translation for calls and media

This upgrade splits into two tracks. Call translation focuses on "person-to-person" scenarios: whether it's a regular phone call or an online meeting, cross-language communication no longer requires everyone to hold up translation software—the glasses take over the job of simultaneous interpretation. Media translation targets "person-to-content" scenarios: for podcasts, online classes, or movies you can't understand, putting on the glasses gives you synchronized translations, removing the copy-and-paste interruption from studying or entertainment. Both tracks point to one conclusion—the value of wearable devices is shifting from light interactions like "reminders and recording" to heavy tasks that truly help people digest information.

Noise resistance and a flagship follow-up

For translation to be accurate, it first has to hear clearly. This update specifically optimizes speech recognition in noisy environments, making simultaneous interpretation more accurate and better able to keep pace—essentially giving the feature a foundation for real-world scenarios. Hardware is moving forward too: after the G1, which went on sale in March this year, Alibaba has introduced the flagship S1, which beats the previous generation across interaction, display, battery life, and hardware configuration. When translation, noise reduction, and a better wearing experience come together, AI glasses are one step closer to being an "everyday external brain."
